title: Why Dago shut down Logology after 5 years: business fundamentals, burnout and going back to a job
summary: Dago explains why he and his wife closed their bootstrapped logo startup Logology after five years: no recurring revenue, constant customer-acquisition pressure, AI uncertainty and a health-wrecking burnout. His main lesson is to start from business fundamentals (demand, willingness to pay, acquisition cost) rather than a cool idea and hard work.

principles.text: Hard work and a good idea don't make a business; only the fundamentals of a good business do.
principles.quote: we were idealistic and thought having a good idea and working hard was enough to succeed

principles.text: Start from the boring business fundamentals: demand, willingness to pay, and customer acquisition cost.
principles.quote: is there demand are customers paying for it enough can you acquire customers at a good enough cost like all the boring

principles.text: Without recurring revenue you must re-win customers every month, which creates relentless pressure.
principles.quote: now because our part doesn't have any recurring Revenue we have to find 100 plus new customers each month this puts us under massive pressure

principles.text: Social proof and audience feedback can feed denial about a struggling business.
principles.quote: because I was like successful on Twitter it could be backed up by other people who thought we were successful so it was kind of like even harder to you know to let go of that

principles.text: Don't sacrifice health and the life you wanted for success at any cost; burnout is a warning sign.
principles.quote: we started sacrificing everything we cared about just to re-success at any cost

principles.text: Next time, build with a co-founder whose skills differ from yours to cover business gaps.
principles.quote: next time I'm doing it with like at least one other person that is completely different from us
